steps.message:
# Diagnose and repair the staged training setup

The workspace holds an asynchronous agentic RL training setup: the framework source, the launcher
and its configuration, the sandbox runtime and the local sandbox service the rollout uses, the
archived console logs and metrics of earlier runs of the same workload on a larger cluster, and the
logs of one run of this workspace.

Determine whether the setup is healthy. If it is not, find the root cause or causes in the code and
configuration, and repair them in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. Do not assume a setting is
causal without connecting it to observed behaviour, and do not stop at the first contributing factor
you find.

**Do not launch training.** Do not start the experiment in the foreground or the background, and do
not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen` or any detach mechanism. The system runs the experiment
itself after you finish; anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap non-training checks
(reading code and logs, `--print-command`, unit-level snippets) are fine.

**Do not use the network.** Diagnose and repair with what is staged locally.

When you are done, submit `/workspace/report.md` with the verdict and the evidence that decides it,
the root cause and the evidence connecting it to the observed behaviour, every file you changed and
what you changed in it, and which metric your fix should move and in which direction. A missing or
empty report scores 0.

## What the system will run

The system clears its own log directory and runs the workspace's launcher as
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B scripts/train_reproduction.py`: the bundled Miles
fully-asynchronous trainer on 8 GPUs (4 training, 4 serving), the pinned Qwen3.5-9B policy, the local
sandbox service, and three rollouts of the staged workload.

The run's shape is fixed and graded from the fresh run's own logs. These workspace files are
byte-compared against pristine copies and must not be modified: everything under `scripts/` and
`runtime/` other than `scripts/run_config.json` — including `runtime/sandbox_service.py`, the
sandbox provider itself, whose latencies and capacity are not yours to change. In
`scripts/run_config.json` only the sandbox client's own environment variables may change; the model,
topology, training and rollout sections are compared against the pristine configuration. Everything
else in the workspace, including `vendor/agent_runtime/` and the vendored framework source, may be
repaired.

Grading requires the run to complete three rollouts with a successful optimizer update each, and to
keep the workload intact: one sandbox per trajectory, every sandbox created, filled and installed
before use, every tool call executed in a sandbox, sandboxes deleted when their trajectory finishes,
and environment errors rare. It then measures the wall-clock time the first two rollouts take. Only
files from this fresh run are graded; do not copy, edit or fabricate metrics.
I'll start by inspecting the staged workspace, launcher config, and prior run logs so I can tell whether the training setup is actually healthy before changing anything.

1→# Asynchronous agentic GRPO workspace

`python3 -B scripts/train_reproduction.py` launches the bundled Miles
fully-asynchronous trainer (Ray + Megatron + SGLang) on a single 8-GPU node:
4 GPUs train the policy (tensor-parallel 2, data-parallel 2) and 4 GPUs serve it as four SGLang engines. The policy is `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, fetched by the prepare stage into `models/`.
`--print-command` prints the exact trainer command line without running it.

The workload is `data/public_repo_tasks.jsonl`, 512 synthetic Python
repositories with one planted defect each, regenerated by the prepare stage
10→with `scripts/build_public_tasks.py`. The policy debugs them with tools
(`list_files`, `read_file`, `search`, `run_tests`, `submit_fix`) over up
to eight turns and is rewarded for naming the defective file and function.
Each trajectory runs in its own sandbox. `runtime/sandbox_service.py` is the local sandbox control plane (create, upload, install, exec, delete over HTTP) that the launcher starts before training; `vendor/agent_runtime/` is the client-side runtime the rollout uses to reach it.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/train_reproduction.py`, `scripts/run_config.json` | launcher and its topology / rollout / training configuration |
20→| `scripts/native_entrypoint.py`, `runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py` | local Ray bootstrap and the Miles async training driver |
| `runtime/rollout.py`, `runtime/fully_async.py` | rollout function: continuous producer, group collection, recycling |
| `runtime/agent_generate.py`, `runtime/environment.py`, `runtime/repo_tools.py` | multi-turn generate function, per-trajectory environment, tools and reward |
| `runtime/training_evidence.py` | before-train-step hook that records every optimizer update |
| `vendor/` | Miles, Miles plugins and Megatron (Core, Bridge) Python source |
| `logs/historical/` | sanitized console logs and derived metrics of the original 16-GPU runs |
| `logs/public_rerun/` | outputs of one run of this workspace on 8 × H800 (layout as below; host names and paths replaced) |
| `scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py` | one-time Hugging Face to Megatron checkpoint conversion run by the launcher |

## Outputs
30→
Each launch writes `experiment_logs/<UTC time>-<pid>/`: `launch.json` (argv and
configuration), `train.log` (full console log), `rollout.<id>.json` (per-rollout
summary), `optimizer/step.<rollout>.<step>.rank<r>.json` (update identity, grad
norm, sampled parameter delta), `turns/*.jsonl` (one record per engine call and
tool batch), `env_setup/*.jsonl` (per-trajectory sandbox setup record) and `sandbox_service.log` / `sandbox_access.jsonl`.

1→# Historical evidence: derivation of the metric files

The metric files in this directory are recomputed from the sanitized console archives by
`python3 derive_metrics.py .` (stdlib only; `--check` verifies the shipped files).
The run configurations are listed in `run_comparison.json`.

## 1. Effective timestamp and windows

`derive_metrics.py` reads `master.log.gz` then `worker.log.gz` of a run in record order. For every record the
10→*effective timestamp* is the first `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` found in `msg`; records without one inherit the last
effective timestamp seen earlier in the same archive (carry-forward). Records before the first embedded
timestamp have none and are only counted in whole-archive aggregates and in reference windows that have no lower
bound. 5-minute windows are `[HH:MM, HH:MM+5)` buckets of the effective timestamp (minute floored to a multiple
of 5). Reference windows (`reference_windows.json`) are half-open `[from, to)`; `null` means unbounded.

## 2. Metric definitions (all line-based; regexes are in `derive_metrics.py`)

| field | source lines | definition |
|---|---|---|
20→| `prefix_hit_rate_pct` | `... Prefill batch, #new-seq: S, #new-token: N, #cached-token: C, ...` | `100 * sum(C) / sum(N + C)` over the printed lines in the window (token-weighted, **not** the mean of per-line ratios; per-line ratios are biased by `chunked_prefill_size=8192` chunking, where only the first chunk of a long prompt can hit). |
| `prefill_new_ktokens`, `prefill_cached_ktokens` | same | `sum(N) / 1000`, `sum(C) / 1000` (3 decimals, i.e. exact token counts expressed in thousands). |
| `prompt_len_p50` | same | median of `N + C` over printed Prefill lines (a chunked long prompt contributes several lines). |
| `running_req_mean_per_engine` / `running_req_max` | `... Decode batch, #running-req: R, #token: K, token usage: U, ... gen throughput (token/s): G, ...` | mean / max of `R` over printed Decode lines, pooled across engines. Each Decode line is one engine's scheduler snapshot. With TP>1 only the TP0 scheduler prints Decode lines. |
| `total_concurrency_est` | same | `running_req_mean_per_engine * rollout_engines`, where `rollout_engines` is the configured engine count from `run_comparison.json`. |
| `sum_of_engine_mean_running_req` | same | group Decode lines by the engine actor pid in the Ray prefix, average `R` per engine, sum over engines seen. Alternative estimate; differs from the above when engines print unevenly or are missing from a window. |
| `engines_seen_in_decode_lines` | same | number of distinct engine pids that printed a Decode line. |
| `gen_throughput_mean_tok_s_per_engine` | same | mean of `G` over printed Decode lines (per-engine decode throughput as SGLang reports it). |
| `kv_token_usage_p50` | same | median of `U` (fraction of the engine's KV token pool in use). |
| `sem_wait_lines`, `sem_wait_p50_s`, `sem_wait_p90_s`, `sem_wait_max_s` | `sandbox setup waited X s for semaphore` | count and linear-interpolated percentiles of `X` over printed lines. The warning is only emitted for waits > 5 s. |
30→| `sem_wait_events_lower_bound` | same | `sum over lines of (N if the line carries "[repeated Nx ...]" else 1)`: Ray folds same-pattern lines from the following ~5 s into one summary line whose N counts the folded occurrences; their values are not printed, so percentiles use printed values only. |
| `slow_generate_*` | `slow agentic generate: turn=T elapsed=E s` | percentiles/max of `E` and `T` over printed lines. The line is only logged for slow LLM calls, so `turn` is the turn index of slow calls (a proxy for trajectory depth). |
| `dropped_group_*` | `[fully-async] Dynamic filter dropped group I (REASON); ...` | `dropped_group_lines` = printed lines; `dropped_groups_distinct_ids_by_reason` = distinct `I` per REASON. Each drop is printed twice in these logs (once per Ray prefix form), hence distinct ids. A dropped group is a *completed* group (all samples finished) that was filtered out; there is no log line for accepted groups, so this is a lower bound on completed groups. |
| `train_steps_ft_distinct`, `first_train_step_ts` | `ft op=train_step rollout=R step=S ...` | distinct `(R, S)` pairs and the earliest effective timestamp. |
| `train_steps_logged_distinct` | `log_utils.py:<n> - step S: {...}` | distinct `S` . |
| `collected_max` | `Warning: No progress for ...s. Queue size: q, Collected: c/n` | max `c` . |
| `train_wait_end_elapsed_s` | `Timer train_wait end (elapsed: X s)` | values of `X` (how long the trainer waited for the first batch). |
| `active_5min_window_spread` | 5-minute windows | min / p50 / max of hit rate, total concurrency and gen throughput over windows with >=10 Prefill and >=10 Decode lines, skipping the first such window (engine warm-up). |

Percentiles use linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy's default "linear" method).
40→
### Caveats that apply to every number

* **Ray de-duplication.** Ray prints the first occurrence of a line pattern (numbers ignored) immediately and
  folds later same-pattern lines from other processes into one `[repeated Nx across cluster]` line. Every
  SGLang Prefill/Decode metric above is therefore computed over a *sample* of scheduler lines (the printed
  ones), not over all scheduler iterations. Weighting by N is not possible for token sums because folded lines'
  numbers are not printed. The engine pid in a folded line's prefix is that of the representative line only.
* Ray also prints some lines with and without the `ip=` part of the prefix; these are different lines unless
  the full text is identical (only the dropped-group lines are systematically doubled).
50→
## 3. Re-deriving

```
python3 -I derive_metrics.py .            # rewrites metrics_summary.json, metrics_windows_5min.{json,csv}
python3 -I derive_metrics.py . --check    # verifies the shipped metric files are reproduced byte-for-byte
```
Stdlib only (Python >= 3.8). `run_comparison.json` supplies the configured engine counts;
`reference_windows.json` the named windows.

`train_async_entrypoint.py` is the Miles asynchronous training driver that
`scripts/native_entrypoint.py` executes inside a local Ray cluster. It creates
the rollout manager (SGLang engines and router), the Megatron actor, performs
the initial weight sync, and then overlaps rollout `k+1` with training on
rollout `k`, syncing weights after every update.

| Location | Source |
10→| --- | --- |
| `train_async_entrypoint.py` | Miles `train_async.py` driver |
| `../fully_async.py`, `../progress_watchdog.py` | continuous rollout producer used by the original runs, generic parts only |
| `../../vendor/miles/`, `../../vendor/miles_plugins/` | Miles `0.2.1.dev1609+g48f39cb4` Python source |
| `../../vendor/megatron/` | Megatron-Core `0.18.0+caeabd765` and Megatron-Bridge `0.5.0` Python source |
| `../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `../../licenses/` | ownership and license notices |

Compiled dependencies (CUDA, Transformer Engine, FlashAttention, SGLang
kernels) come from the task image; bundled Python source takes precedence on
`PYTHONPATH`.

1→"""Local sandbox control plane used by the public rollout.

The service models the remote sandbox provider the original run used: creating
a sandbox, uploading the repository, installing tool commands, executing tool
calls and deleting the sandbox are separate HTTP operations with their own
latency.  Provisioning slows down as more sandboxes are being created at once,
which is how the hosted provider behaved under burst load.  All latencies come
from a seeded generator and every request is appended to a JSONL access log.

40→                                   "live": len(self.sandboxes), "provisioning": self.provisioning, **extra}) + "
")

    def _latency(self, median: float) -> float:
        return median * self.rng.lognormvariate(0.0, self.options.sigma)

    async def create(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        started = time.time()
        body = await request.json()
        self.provisioning += 1
        try:
50→            contention = 1.0 + self.provisioning / self.options.provider_capacity
            await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.create_s) * contention)
        finally:
            self.provisioning -= 1
        sandbox_id = f"sbx-{next(self.ids):06d}"
        self.sandboxes[sandbox_id] = {"template": body.get("template"), "files": {}, "test_failure": "", "commands": False}
        self.counters["created"] += 1
        self._record("create", started, sandbox=sandbox_id)

        started = time.time()
80→        sandbox = self._get(request)
        await asyncio.sleep(self._latency(self.options.install_s))

100→        started = time.time()

        self.counters["deleted"] += 1
        self._record("delete", started, sandbox=request.match_info["sid"])
        return web.json_response({"ok": True})

    parser.add_argument("--exec-s", type=float, default=0.4)
    parser.add_argument("--delete-s", type=float, default=0.3)
    parser.add_argument("--sigma", type=float, default=0.45)
    parser.add_argument("--provider-capacity", type=float, default=48.0)
    return parser.parse_args(argv)

    opts.access_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

import argparse
import time
from copy import deepcopy

from miles.rollout.base_types import GenerateFnInput, GenerateFnOutput

20→)
from miles.utils.lifecycle import TrajectoryLifecycle
from miles.utils.misc import load_function


async def generate(input: GenerateFnInput) -> GenerateFnOutput:
    # ----------------------- Setup -------------------------

    args = input.args
    sample = deepcopy(input.sample)
30→    tokenizer = input.state.tokenizer
    assert not args.partial_rollout, "Partial rollout is not supported"

    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    execute_tool_function = load_function(args.generate_execute_tool_function_path)

    tool_specs = load_function(args.generate_tool_specs_path)
    tool_call_parser = create_tool_call_parser(tool_specs, args.generate_tool_call_parser)

40→    # tool-call markup stays inline in the assistant text (what the model emitted)
    record_trajectory = args.save_debug_trajectory_data is not None
    trajectory = (list(sample.prompt) if isinstance(sample.prompt, list) else []) if record_trajectory else None

    # ----------------------- Initial prompts -------------------------

    prompt_tokens_ids = compute_prompt_ids_from_sample(input.state, sample, tools=tool_specs)

    sample.tokens = prompt_tokens_ids.copy()

50→    for _turn in range(args.generate_max_turns):
        # ----------------------- Call inference endpoint -------------------------

        payload, halt_status = compute_request_payload(args, sample.tokens, input.sampling_params)
        if payload is None:
            sample.status = halt_status
            break

        gen_t0 = time.time()
        output = await input.state.engine_transport(url, payload, headers=compute_routing_headers(args, sample))
60→        sink = None if input.evaluation else TrajectoryLifecycle().sink
        if sink is not None:
            tokens = output.get("meta_info", {}).get("completion_tokens", "")
            sink.gen_span(sample, gen_t0, time.time(), turn=_turn + 1, detail=str(tokens))
        await update_sample_from_response(args, sample, payload=payload, output=output, update_loss_mask=True)
        if record_trajectory:
            trajectory.append({"role": "assistant", "content": output["text"]})
            sample.metadata["messages"] = list(trajectory)  # snapshot: trajectory keeps growing in later turns

        if output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"] in ("abort", "length"):
70→            break

        # ----------------------- Execute tools -------------------------

        _, tool_calls = tool_call_parser.parse_non_stream(output["text"])
        if len(tool_calls) == 0:
            break

        tool_t0 = time.time()
        tool_messages = await execute_tool_calls(tool_calls, execute_tool_function)
80→        if sink is not None:
            sink.tool_span(sample, tool_t0, time.time(), turn=_turn + 1, detail=f"{len(tool_calls)} calls")
        update_sample_with_tool_responses(sample, tool_messages, tokenizer=tokenizer)
        if record_trajectory:
            trajectory.extend(tool_messages)
            sample.metadata["messages"] = list(trajectory)

    return GenerateFnOutput(samples=sample)

    parser.add_argument("--generate-max-turns", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--generate-tool-specs-path", type=str)
    parser.add_argument("--generate-tool-call-parser", type=str)
    parser.add_argument("--generate-execute-tool-function-path", type=str)


generate.add_arguments = _add_arguments

python3 - << 'PY'
"""Simulate sandbox lifecycle under different client policies using recorded server latencies.

We don't re-simulate RNG; we use empirical duration distributions from the access log
but the contention multiplier is inside recorded durations already. Better: implement
a discrete-event sim of the SERVICE itself (same formulas) plus client policies,
seeded the same way, to estimate wall clock of N trajectories.

Service:
  create: latency(6.0)* (1 + provisioning/48), provisioning incremented during create
  upload: latency(1.5)*(1+size/200000)  -- unknown sizes, use median factor ~1.2 from data? 
  install: latency(2.0)
  exec: latency(0.4)
  delete: latency(0.3)
  sigma 0.45, seed 20261110
  single-threaded event loop but sleeps are async so concurrent.

Client policies to compare:
A) current: semaphore 32 held for create+upload+install; httpx pool 20; tool calls share pool; inflight groups 32 * 8 samples = 256 trajectories trying to set up but sem 32
B) release semaphore before holding long? 
C) limit concurrent creates to ~provider capacity sweet spot
D) separate connection pools for setup vs exec
E) don't share 20 conns

Also check: max concurrent server ops is exactly 20 = SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS. So the pool is the bottleneck that caps server concurrency at 20. Creates take the slots.

If we raise pool, create concurrency could go to semaphore 32, worsening create contention (provisioning/capacity).

provider_capacity=48, contention = 1 + provisioning/48.
At provisioning=20, multiplier=1.42; at 32, 1.67; at 8, 1.17. Not huge vs the 6s base. The BIG cost is client queueing: create HTTP waits ~10s extra because pool is full of other creates.

And tool calls wait behind creates for a free connection: tool latency mean 13s vs exec 0.45s.

Fix direction:
1. Separate http pools OR priority so exec/delete don't wait behind creates? Or raise max connections so tools aren't blocked.
2. Limit concurrent creates so each create is faster AND connections free for tools.
3. Lower inflight so fewer simultaneous sandboxes... but grading wants speed of first two rollouts. More parallelism of generation is good IF tools aren't stuck.

If we set max_connections high (e.g. 512) AND limit concurrent creates to something like 8-16:
- creates don't pile up (contention modest)
- tools get connections immediately (0.45s)
- uploads/installs also concurrent

Semaphore currently 32 covering whole setup. 32 concurrent setups * ~12s setup = high. 
With separate create limit of K:

Let me simulate wall clock for one rollout of 128 trajectories, each:
  setup: create, upload, install
  then ~5 tool calls (exec) sequential with think time? Generation is on GPU and was mean 4s but that's also queued. For sandbox-only, generation overlaps.

The graded metric is wall clock of first two rollouts. Sandbox is a big fraction if tools are 13s * 5 turns = 65s per trajectory serialized on tools, plus gen ~4s*5. With 256 inflight and 4 engines, gen concurrency is limited by engines.

Turn trace: max concurrent tool batches 129, gen latency p50 1.8s. So GPUs are not the only stall; tools add 13s between turns.

If tools drop from 13s to 0.5s, inter-turn gap shrinks by ~12s * ~5 turns = 60s per trajectory. With high parallelism, rollout wall might be dominated by the slowest trajectory critical path rather than sum.

Critical path per trajectory: setup_queue + create + upload + install + sum(gen + tool).
If many run in parallel, wall ~= time until 128 finish, with producer keeping 256 inflight but only 32 setup at a time.

Let me simulate more carefully with an event loop.
"""
import asyncio, random, time, math, statistics

SEED=20261110
CREATE_S=6.0
UPLOAD_S=1.5
INSTALL_S=2.0
EXEC_S=0.4
DELETE_S=0.3
SIGMA=0.45
CAP=48.0

# empirical file size factor from access log: upload duration / lognorm
# We'll just use size=0 for relative comparison, or sample a typical multiplier.
# From data upload mean 1.79 vs expected median 1.5 * E[lognorm]. 
# E[lognorm(0,0.45)] = exp(0.45**2/2)=1.106
# so size factor mean ~ 1.79/(1.5*1.106)=1.08. Small. Ignore size.

class Svc:
    def __init__(self, seed=SEED):
        self.rng=random.Random(seed)
        self.prov=0
        self.live=0
        self.ops={"create":0,"upload":0,"install":0,"exec":0,"delete":0}
    def lat(self, med):
        return med*self.rng.lognormvariate(0, SIGMA)
    async def create(self):
        self.prov+=1
        try:
            d=self.lat(CREATE_S)*(1+self.prov/CAP)
            await asyncio.sleep(d)
        finally:
            self.prov-=1
        self.live+=1
        self.ops["create"]+=1
        return d
    async def upload(self):
        d=self.lat(UPLOAD_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["upload"]+=1; return d
    async def install(self):
        d=self.lat(INSTALL_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["install"]+=1; return d
    async def exec(self):
        d=self.lat(EXEC_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["exec"]+=1; return d
    async def delete(self):
        d=self.lat(DELETE_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.live-=1; self.ops["delete"]+=1; return d

async def run_policy(name, n_traj=128, turns=5, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, create_limit=None, separate_exec_pool=False, gen_s=2.0, inflight=256):
    svc=Svc()
    setup_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(sem_n)
    pool=asyncio.Semaphore(pool_n)  # shared connections
    exec_pool=asyncio.Semaphore(pool_n if not separate_exec_pool else 256)
    create_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(create_limit or 10**9)
    inflight_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(inflight)
    tool_lats=[]
    setup_walls=[]
    done_at=[]
    t0=time.perf_counter()  # not used; use asyncio loop time
    start=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()

    async def with_pool(coro_fn, poolsem):
        async with poolsem:
            return await coro_fn()

    async def one(i):
        async with inflight_sem:
            t_setup=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
            async with setup_sem:
                async with create_sem:
                    await with_pool(svc.create, pool)
                await with_pool(svc.upload, pool)
                await with_pool(svc.install, pool)
            setup_walls.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-t_setup)
            for _ in range(turns):
                await asyncio.sleep(gen_s)  # GPU think, no sandbox conn
                t1=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                await with_pool(svc.exec, exec_pool if separate_exec_pool else pool)
                tool_lats.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-t1)
            await with_pool(svc.delete, exec_pool if separate_exec_pool else pool)
            done_at.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-start)

    await asyncio.gather(*[one(i) for i in range(n_traj)])
    end=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-start
    def pct(xs,p):
        xs=sorted(xs); return xs[int((len(xs)-1)*p)]
    print(f"{name:40} wall={end:7.1f}s setup_p50={pct(setup_walls,.5):6.1f} tool_p50={pct(tool_lats,.5):5.2f} tool_mean={sum(tool_lats)/len(tool_lats):5.2f} live_end={svc.live} creates={svc.ops['create']}")

async def main():
    # current-like: 256 want to start, sem 32, pool 20, 128 traj, 5 tools, gen 2s
    await run_policy("current sem32 pool20 inflight256", sem_n=32, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem32 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=32, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem8 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=8, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem16 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=16, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem32 pool20 + sep exec", sem_n=32, pool_n=20, separate_exec_pool=True, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem16 pool64 create_limit8", sem_n=16, pool_n=64, create_limit=8, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem48 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=48, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("no sem pool256 inflight128", sem_n=1000, pool_n=256, inflight=128, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("no sem pool20 inflight256", sem_n=1000, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    # two rollouts back to back of 128, producer keeps running - approximate 256 traj
    await run_policy("current 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 sem16 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=16, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 sem8 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=8, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 nosem 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=1000, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create8 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=8, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create4 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=4, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create12 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=12, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)

asyncio.run(main())

"""Simulate sandbox lifecycle under different client policies using recorded server latencies.

We don't re-simulate RNG; we use empirical duration distributions from the access log
but the contention multiplier is inside recorded durations already. Better: implement
a discrete-event sim of the SERVICE itself (same formulas) plus client policies,
seeded the same way, to estimate wall clock of N trajectories.

Service:
  create: latency(6.0)* (1 + provisioning/48), provisioning incremented during create
  upload: latency(1.5)*(1+size/200000)  -- unknown sizes, use median factor ~1.2 from data? 
  install: latency(2.0)
  exec: latency(0.4)
  delete: latency(0.3)
  sigma 0.45, seed 20261110
  single-threaded event loop but sleeps are async so concurrent.

Client policies to compare:
A) current: semaphore 32 held for create+upload+install; httpx pool 20; tool calls share pool; inflight groups 32 * 8 samples = 256 trajectories trying to set up but sem 32
B) release semaphore before holding long? 
C) limit concurrent creates to ~provider capacity sweet spot
D) separate connection pools for setup vs exec
E) don't share 20 conns

Also check: max concurrent server ops is exactly 20 = SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS. So the pool is the bottleneck that caps server concurrency at 20. Creates take the slots.

If we raise pool, create concurrency could go to semaphore 32, worsening create contention (provisioning/capacity).

provider_capacity=48, contention = 1 + provisioning/48.
At provisioning=20, multiplier=1.42; at 32, 1.67; at 8, 1.17. Not huge vs the 6s base. The BIG cost is client queueing: create HTTP waits ~10s extra because pool is full of other creates.

And tool calls wait behind creates for a free connection: tool latency mean 13s vs exec 0.45s.

Fix direction:
1. Separate http pools OR priority so exec/delete don't wait behind creates? Or raise max connections so tools aren't blocked.
2. Limit concurrent creates so each create is faster AND connections free for tools.
3. Lower inflight so fewer simultaneous sandboxes... but grading wants speed of first two rollouts. More parallelism of generation is good IF tools aren't stuck.

If we set max_connections high (e.g. 512) AND limit concurrent creates to something like 8-16:
- creates don't pile up (contention modest)
- tools get connections immediately (0.45s)
- uploads/installs also concurrent

Semaphore currently 32 covering whole setup. 32 concurrent setups * ~12s setup = high. 
With separate create limit of K:

Let me simulate wall clock for one rollout of 128 trajectories, each:
  setup: create, upload, install
  then ~5 tool calls (exec) sequential with think time? Generation is on GPU and was mean 4s but that's also queued. For sandbox-only, generation overlaps.

The graded metric is wall clock of first two rollouts. Sandbox is a big fraction if tools are 13s * 5 turns = 65s per trajectory serialized on tools, plus gen ~4s*5. With 256 inflight and 4 engines, gen concurrency is limited by engines.

Turn trace: max concurrent tool batches 129, gen latency p50 1.8s. So GPUs are not the only stall; tools add 13s between turns.

If tools drop from 13s to 0.5s, inter-turn gap shrinks by ~12s * ~5 turns = 60s per trajectory. With high parallelism, rollout wall might be dominated by the slowest trajectory critical path rather than sum.

Critical path per trajectory: setup_queue + create + upload + install + sum(gen + tool).
If many run in parallel, wall ~= time until 128 finish, with producer keeping 256 inflight but only 32 setup at a time.

Let me simulate more carefully with an event loop.
"""
import asyncio, random, time, math, statistics

SEED=20261110
CREATE_S=6.0
UPLOAD_S=1.5
INSTALL_S=2.0
EXEC_S=0.4
DELETE_S=0.3
SIGMA=0.45
CAP=48.0

# empirical file size factor from access log: upload duration / lognorm
# We'll just use size=0 for relative comparison, or sample a typical multiplier.
# From data upload mean 1.79 vs expected median 1.5 * E[lognorm]. 
# E[lognorm(0,0.45)] = exp(0.45**2/2)=1.106
# so size factor mean ~ 1.79/(1.5*1.106)=1.08. Small. Ignore size.

class Svc:
    def __init__(self, seed=SEED):
        self.rng=random.Random(seed)
        self.prov=0
        self.live=0
        self.ops={"create":0,"upload":0,"install":0,"exec":0,"delete":0}
    def lat(self, med):
        return med*self.rng.lognormvariate(0, SIGMA)
    async def create(self):
        self.prov+=1
        try:
            d=self.lat(CREATE_S)*(1+self.prov/CAP)
            await asyncio.sleep(d)
        finally:
            self.prov-=1
        self.live+=1
        self.ops["create"]+=1
        return d
    async def upload(self):
        d=self.lat(UPLOAD_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["upload"]+=1; return d
    async def install(self):
        d=self.lat(INSTALL_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["install"]+=1; return d
    async def exec(self):
        d=self.lat(EXEC_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.ops["exec"]+=1; return d
    async def delete(self):
        d=self.lat(DELETE_S)
        await asyncio.sleep(d); self.live-=1; self.ops["delete"]+=1; return d

async def run_policy(name, n_traj=128, turns=5, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, create_limit=None, separate_exec_pool=False, gen_s=2.0, inflight=256):
    svc=Svc()
    setup_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(sem_n)
    pool=asyncio.Semaphore(pool_n)  # shared connections
    exec_pool=asyncio.Semaphore(pool_n if not separate_exec_pool else 256)
    create_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(create_limit or 10**9)
    inflight_sem=asyncio.Semaphore(inflight)
    tool_lats=[]
    setup_walls=[]
    done_at=[]
    t0=time.perf_counter()  # not used; use asyncio loop time
    start=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()

    async def with_pool(coro_fn, poolsem):
        async with poolsem:
            return await coro_fn()

    async def one(i):
        async with inflight_sem:
            t_setup=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
            async with setup_sem:
                async with create_sem:
                    await with_pool(svc.create, pool)
                await with_pool(svc.upload, pool)
                await with_pool(svc.install, pool)
            setup_walls.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-t_setup)
            for _ in range(turns):
                await asyncio.sleep(gen_s)  # GPU think, no sandbox conn
                t1=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                await with_pool(svc.exec, exec_pool if separate_exec_pool else pool)
                tool_lats.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-t1)
            await with_pool(svc.delete, exec_pool if separate_exec_pool else pool)
            done_at.append(asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-start)

    await asyncio.gather(*[one(i) for i in range(n_traj)])
    end=asyncio.get_event_loop().time()-start
    def pct(xs,p):
        xs=sorted(xs); return xs[int((len(xs)-1)*p)]
    print(f"{name:40} wall={end:7.1f}s setup_p50={pct(setup_walls,.5):6.1f} tool_p50={pct(tool_lats,.5):5.2f} tool_mean={sum(tool_lats)/len(tool_lats):5.2f} live_end={svc.live} creates={svc.ops['create']}")

async def main():
    # current-like: 256 want to start, sem 32, pool 20, 128 traj, 5 tools, gen 2s
    await run_policy("current sem32 pool20 inflight256", sem_n=32, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem32 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=32, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem8 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=8, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem16 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=16, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem32 pool20 + sep exec", sem_n=32, pool_n=20, separate_exec_pool=True, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem16 pool64 create_limit8", sem_n=16, pool_n=64, create_limit=8, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("sem48 pool256 inflight256", sem_n=48, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("no sem pool256 inflight128", sem_n=1000, pool_n=256, inflight=128, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("no sem pool20 inflight256", sem_n=1000, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    # two rollouts back to back of 128, producer keeps running - approximate 256 traj
    await run_policy("current 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 sem16 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=16, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 sem8 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=8, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("pool256 nosem 256 traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=1000, pool_n=256, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create8 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=8, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create4 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=4, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)
    await run_policy("create12 sem64 pool256 256traj", n_traj=256, sem_n=64, pool_n=256, create_limit=12, inflight=256, gen_s=1.8)

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
# use a fast virtual clock by monkeypatching? asyncio sleep is real.
# Scale all sleeps by 100x via wrapping — still slow for 256* (setup+5*2s).
# 256 traj * ~20s = but parallel, wall ~100s real. Too slow.
# Implement a tiny discrete event sim instead.
import heapq, random, statistics

SEED=20261110
CREATE,UPLOAD,INSTALL,EXEC,DELETE=6.0,1.5,2.0,0.4,0.3
SIGMA=0.45
CAP=48.0

class Sim:
    def __init__(self):
        self.t=0.0
        self.q=[]
        self.seq=0
    def sleep(self, dt, cb):
        self.seq+=1
        heapq.heappush(self.q,(self.t+dt, self.seq, cb))
    def run(self):
        while self.q:
            self.t, _, cb = heapq.heappop(self.q)
            cb()

def simulate(n_traj=256, turns=5, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, create_limit=None, sep_exec=False, gen_s=1.8, inflight=256, exec_pool_n=256):
    rng=random.Random(SEED)
    def lat(med):
        return med*rng.lognormvariate(0,SIGMA)
    sim=Sim()
    # resource counters
    state={"prov":0,"live":0,"setup_held":0,"pool":0,"exec_pool":0,"create_held":0,"inflight":0,
           "setup_waiters":[],"pool_waiters":[],"exec_waiters":[],"create_waiters":[],"inflight_waiters":[]}
    tool_lats=[]
    setup_walls=[]
    done=[]
    max_live=0
    max_prov=0

    def acquire(waiters, held_key, limit, cont):
        if state[held_key] < limit:
            state[held_key]+=1
            cont()
        else:
            waiters.append(cont)
    def release(waiters, held_key):
        if waiters:
            # transfer to next waiter, keep held count
            cont=waiters.pop(0)
            sim.sleep(0, cont)
        else:
            state[held_key]-=1

    def start_one(i):
        def got_inflight():
            t_setup=sim.t
            def got_setup():
                def after_create_slot():
                    # take pool for create
                    def got_pool_create():
                        state["prov"]+=1
                        nonlocal max_prov
                        max_prov=max(max_prov, state["prov"])
                        d=lat(CREATE)*(1+state["prov"]/CAP)
                        def done_create():
                            state["prov"]-=1
                            state["live"]+=1
                            nonlocal max_live
                            max_live=max(max_live, state["live"])
                            release(state["pool_waiters"], "pool")
                            release(state["create_waiters"], "create_held")
                            # upload
                            def got_pool_up():
                                d2=lat(UPLOAD)
                                def done_up():
                                    release(state["pool_waiters"], "pool")
                                    def got_pool_in():
                                        d3=lat(INSTALL)
                                        def done_in():
                                            release(state["pool_waiters"], "pool")
                                            release(state["setup_waiters"], "setup_held")
                                            setup_walls.append(sim.t-t_setup)
                                            do_turns(0)
                                        sim.sleep(d3, done_in)
                                    acquire(state["pool_waiters"], "pool", pool_n, got_pool_in)
                                sim.sleep(d2, done_up)
                            acquire(state["pool_waiters"], "pool", pool_n, got_pool_up)
                        sim.sleep(d, done_create)
                    acquire(state["pool_waiters"], "pool", pool_n, got_pool_create)
                lim = create_limit if create_limit else 10**9
                acquire(state["create_waiters"], "create_held", lim, after_create_slot)
            acquire(state["setup_waiters"], "setup_held", sem_n, got_setup)

            def do_turns(k):
                if k==turns:
                    def got_del():
                        d=lat(DELETE)
                        def done_del():
                            state["live"]-=1
                            if sep_exec:
                                release(state["exec_waiters"], "exec_pool")
                            else:
                                release(state["pool_waiters"], "pool")
                            release(state["inflight_waiters"], "inflight")
                            done.append(sim.t)

import gzip, json, collections
# reconstruct per-sandbox timeline of server ops and compare to a sample session's tool times
# pick one sandbox that has execs and match to env setup session

events=[]
with gzip.open("/workspace/logs/public_rerun/sandbox_access.jsonl.gz") as f:
    for line in f:
        events.append(json.loads(line))

# group by sandbox
by=collections.defaultdict(list)
for o in events:
    if "sandbox" in o:
        by[o["sandbox"]].append(o)

# find a sandbox with several execs
cands=sorted(by, key=lambda s: -sum(1 for o in by[s] if o["op"]=="exec"))
sid=cands[10]
print("sandbox", sid)
for o in by[sid]:
    print(f"  {o['op']:8} t={o['t']:.3f} dur={o['duration_s']:.3f} live={o['live']} prov={o['provisioning']}")

# client setup record
recs=[]
with gzip.open("/workspace/logs/public_rerun/env_setup/env_setup.6329.jsonl.gz") as f:
    for line in f:
        r=json.loads(line)
        if r.get("sandbox_id")==sid:
            recs.append(r)
print("setup recs", recs)

# turns for that session
if recs:
    sess=recs[0]["session"]
    print("session", sess)
    with gzip.open("/workspace/logs/public_rerun/turns/turns.6329.jsonl.gz") as f:
        for line in f:
            o=json.loads(line)
            if o.get("session")==sess:
                print(o["event"], {k:o[k] for k in o if k not in ("session",)})

# How many requests are waiting: estimate client-side in-flight HTTP by assuming
# client start ~= server start - queue. We can't see queue directly.
# Count overlapping server ops == connections in use (max 20). When at 20, new requests queue.
# Compute fraction of time the server has >=18 concurrent ops, and average queue depth if we knew arrivals.

# Estimate arrival process of client requests from env_setup start? 
# Alternative: compute for each exec, how many other ops were in their server-active window — if <20, exec shouldn't queue unless queued BEFORE server start.
# Client tool latency = queue + server duration. server mean 0.45, client mean 13 => queue ~12.6
# If pool is 20 and saturated, queue is real.

# saturation: fraction of timeline with concurrent server ops == 20
iv=[]
for o in events:
    iv.append((o["t"],1))
    iv.append((o["t"]+o["duration_s"],-1))
iv.sort()
# integrate time at each level
from collections import defaultdict
time_at=defaultdict(float)
cur=0
prev=iv[0][0]
for t,d in iv:
    time_at[cur]+=t-prev
    cur+=d
    prev=t
total=sum(time_at.values())
print("time fraction by concurrency (top):")
for k in sorted(time_at):
    if time_at[k]/total>0.01 or k>=18:
        print(f"  {k:3d}: {time_at[k]:7.1f}s  {100*time_at[k]/total:5.1f}%")
print("total span", total)

    args_dict: dict,

    api_keys = args_dict.get("control_plane_api_keys", [])

    audit_enabled = args_dict.get("control_plane_audit_enabled", False)

import heapq, random
SEED=20261110
CREATE,UPLOAD,INSTALL,EXEC,DELETE=6.0,1.5,2.0,0.4,0.3
SIGMA=0.45
CAP=48.0

def simulate(n_traj=660, turns=5, sem_n=32, pool_n=20, gen_s=1.8, inflight=256, label=""):
    rng=random.Random(SEED)
    def lat(med):
        return med*rng.lognormvariate(0,SIGMA)
    t=0.0
    q=[]; seq=0
    def sleep(dt, cb):
        nonlocal seq
        seq+=1
        heapq.heappush(q,(t+dt, seq, cb))
    state={"prov":0,"setup":0,"pool":0,"inflight":0,"live":0,
           "sw":[],"pw":[],"iw":[], "max_live":0,"max_prov":0,
           "sat_time":0.0,"last":0.0}
    # track saturation coarsely: not exact integral
    tool=[]; setup_w=[]; sem_wait=[]
    def acquire(waiters, key, limit, cont, wait_acc=None):
        if state[key] < limit:
            state[key]+=1
            if wait_acc is not None:
                wait_acc.append(0.0)
            cont()
        else:
            waiters.append((t, cont, wait_acc))
    def release(waiters, key):
        if waiters:
            ts, cont, wait_acc = waiters.pop(0)
            if wait_acc is not None:
                wait_acc.append(t-ts)
            state[key]+=0  # keep held, transfer
            sleep(0, cont)
        else:
            state[key]-=1
    def start(i):
        def got_inf():
            holder={"t0":0}
            def got_setup():
                holder["t0"]=t
                def got_pc():
                    state["prov"]+=1
                    state["max_prov"]=max(state["max_prov"], state["prov"])
                    d=lat(CREATE)*(1+state["prov"]/CAP)
                    def done_c():
                        state["prov"]-=1
                        state["live"]+=1
                        state["max_live"]=max(state["max_live"], state["live"])
                        release(state["pw"],"pool")
                        def got_pu():
                            d2=lat(UPLOAD)
                            def done_u():
                                release(state["pw"],"pool")
                                def got_pi():
                                    d3=lat(INSTALL)
                                    def done_i():
                                        release(state["pw"],"pool")
                                        release(state["sw"],"setup")
                                        setup_w.append(t-holder["t0"])
                                        turns_fn(0)
                                    sleep(d3, done_i)
                                acquire(state["pw"],"pool",pool_n, got_pi)
                            sleep(d2, done_u)
                        acquire(state["pw"],"pool",pool_n, got_pu)
                    sleep(d, done_c)
                acquire(state["pw"],"pool",pool_n, got_pc)
            acquire(state["sw"],"setup",sem_n, got_setup, sem_wait)
            def turns_fn(k):
                if k==turns:
                    def got_d():
                        d=lat(DELETE)
                        def done_d():
                            state["live"]-=1
                            release(state["pw"],"pool")
                            release(state["iw"],"inflight")
                        sleep(d, done_d)
                    acquire(state["pw"],"pool",pool_n, got_d)
                    return
                def after_gen():
                    t1=t
                    def got_e():
                        d=lat(EXEC)
                        def done_e():
                            tool.append(t-t1)
                            release(state["pw"],"pool")
                            turns_fn(k+1)
                        sleep(d, done_e)
                    acquire(state["pw"],"pool",pool_n, got_e)
                sleep(gen_s, after_gen)
        acquire(state["iw"],"inflight",inflight, got_inf)
    for i in range(n_traj):
        start(i)
    while q:
        t,_,cb=heapq.heappop(q)
        cb()
    def pct(xs,p):
        xs=sorted(xs); return xs[int((len(xs)-1)*p)] if xs else None
    print(f"{label:48} wall={t:7.1f} sem_p50={pct(sem_wait,.5):6.1f} setup_p50={pct(setup_w,.5):6.1f} tool_mean={sum(tool)/len(tool):5.2f} tool_p50={pct(tool,.5):5.2f} max_live={state['max_live']} max_prov={state['max_prov']} ntool={len(tool)}")

print("match real ~660 traj")
simulate(label="OLD sem32 pool20")
simulate(sem_n=48, pool_n=512, label="NEW sem48 pool512")
simulate(sem_n=64, pool_n=512, label="sem64 pool512")
simulate(sem_n=96, pool_n=512, label="sem96 pool512")
simulate(sem_n=32, pool_n=512, label="sem32 pool512")
simulate(sem_n=48, pool_n=128, label="sem48 pool128")
# gen slower
print("--- gen 4 ---")
simulate(gen_s=4.0, label="OLD gen4")
simulate(sem_n=48, pool_n=512, gen_s=4.0, label="NEW gen4")
simulate(sem_n=64, pool_n=512, gen_s=4.0, label="sem64 gen4")

# a handful of setup calls.

SANDBOX_KEEPALIVE_EXPIRY = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_KEEPALIVE_EXPIRY", "30"))
# Create latency grows with the number of sandboxes the provider is
# provisioning at once (about 6s at idle, tens of seconds under a burst) and
20→# the call also waits for a free connection. 60s aborted those creates.
SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "180"))
SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT", "180"))

arguments.content:
# Verdict

The staged training setup is not healthy. The public 8-GPU rerun does complete three rollouts and three successful optimizer updates, and it keeps the workload shape (one sandbox per trajectory, create then upload then install before any exec, tool calls inside a sandbox, environment errors absent). It is slow for a reason in the client, not in the model or the trainer: sandbox tool calls spend most of their time queued on a 20-connection HTTP pool that setup creates never release.

The wall-clock of the first two rollouts is the graded quantity. In `logs/public_rerun/rollout.0.json` and `rollout.1.json` those are **234.8 s** and **76.8 s**. A discrete-event replay of the sandbox service (same latency formula as `runtime/sandbox_service.py`) puts the repaired client at roughly half that sandbox-bound time. Training was not launched.

# Evidence the run itself is intact

From `logs/public_rerun/`:

- `rollout.0.json`, `rollout.1.json`, `rollout.2.json`: 16 groups / 128 samples each, `abort_reasons` empty, rewards 0.92 / 0.81 / 0.90.

- `logs/public_rerun/turns` has no `env_error`. Tool execution is not failing; it is waiting.
- Optimizer steps succeed and grad norms are finite. This is not a training-numerics failure.
- The sandbox service's latencies and capacity are fixed by the task and were not changed. The diagnosis uses them only as the formula that turns client concurrency into create time.

# Repair

Client environment variables, forwarded by the existing launcher (`cfg["env"]` is copied into the process env and listed in `FORWARD_ENV`). Defaults in the client match, so a path that forgets the env still behaves.

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vendor/agent_runtime/sandbox_client.py` | Default `SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS` 20 → 512, `SANDBOX_MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS` 20 → 256, `SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` 60 → 180, `SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT` 30 → 180. |
| `vendor/agent_runtime/env_runtime.py` | Default `MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP` no longer follows `SANDBOX_OPERATION_CONCURRENCY` (32). It is 64. |
| `scripts/run_config.json` | Only the `env` object: added `SANDBOX_MAX_CONNECTIONS=512`, `SANDBOX_MAX_KEEPALIVE_CONNECTIONS=256`, `SANDBOX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=180`, `SANDBOX_POOL_TIMEOUT=180`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_SANDBOX_SETUP=64`. Model, topology, training, rollout, router and services are unchanged. |

`runtime/agent_generate.py` was edited while testing a routing-key pin and restored; it matches the staged file again.

Why 512 and 64: a discrete-event replay of this service (create/upload/install/exec/delete formula, seed 20261110, σ=0.45, capacity 48, 256 trajectories, 5 tool turns, 1.8 s of generation between turns, inflight 256) gives:

- old client (setup 32, pool 20): wall **206 s**, tool p50 **4.1 s** (the replay understates the real 13 s tool wait because it also gives every turn a free generation slot; in the trace, generation and tools share the stall)
- pool 512, setup semaphore 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / uncapped: wall **132 / 103 / 99 / 92 / 158 s**, tool p50 **0.40 s** in every pooled case
- 660 trajectories (the number of generate sessions in the rerun), pool 512, setup 64: wall **221 s** against **501 s** for the old client

64 is the knee: faster than 48, and 96 is only slightly faster while pushing create concurrency to 96 (multiplier ~3). 512 connections is enough that exec and delete never queue behind create (the replay's tool time falls to the server's 0.4 s at a pool of 128 already; 512 covers 256 in-flight trajectories with a setup call and a tool call outstanding). The 180 s timeouts cover a contended create without turning a slow provider into an `env_error` abort.

`python3 -B scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command` still builds the trainer argv. Training was not started.

# Metric the fix should move

**Rollout wall-clock of the first two rollouts, down.**

In the graded run that is `rollout.0.json` `wall_s` plus `rollout.1.json` `wall_s` (234.845 + 76.805 = 311.7 s in the staged rerun). The mechanism is tool-batch latency in `turns/*.jsonl` falling from a mean of 13.1 s toward the server exec time of ~0.45 s, and `env_setup` `create_s` falling because creates no longer wait ~10 s for a connection. Setup semaphore waits will remain (64 slots, 256 trajectories) but each admitted create should stay near 1 + 64/48 ≈ 2.3× the idle 6 s rather than queueing the whole pool.

Prefix-cache hit rate is not the metric this change targets. Environment-error rate should stay near zero; the longer timeouts are there so the larger admission window does not start aborting creates.

steps.message:
The setup was healthy enough to finish three rollouts and three optimizer updates, but the first two rollouts were slow because sandbox tool calls sat in a 20-connection HTTP pool. That is repaired in the client, and training was not started.

The public rerun shows the stall directly. Server execs average 0.45 s, while client tool batches average 13.1 s. The sandbox service was at exactly 20 in-flight operations for 90.6% of the run, which is the old pool size. Client create time also ran about 10 s above the server create time on the same sandbox ids. Setup admission was capped at 32 and held across create, upload, and install, so those long creates filled the pool and tool calls waited behind them.

Changes:

- `vendor/agent_runtime/sandbox_client.py`: connection pool 20 → 512, keepalive 256, request and pool timeouts 60/30 s → 180 s.
- `vendor/agent_runtime/env_runtime.py`: setup admission 32 → 64, matched to the provider’s create-capacity curve.
- `scripts/run_config.json`: the same values in `env` only. Model, topology, training, and rollout are unchanged.

A discrete-event replay of the sandbox service drops the sandbox-bound time from about 206 s to about 99 s for 256 trajectories, with tool time back at the server’s 0.4 s. The metric that should move is the wall-clock of the first two rollouts, down from 234.8 s + 76.8 s. Details and the evidence are in `report.md`.
